'''John Mackintosh Howie''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE|FRSE}} (23 May 1936 – 26 December 2011) was a [[Scotland|Scottish]] [[mathematician]] and prominent [[semigroup theory|semigroup theorist]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.scotsman.com/news/obituaries/obituary_professor_john_howie_academic_who_helped_reform_scottish_education_1_2072053 |title=Obituary: Professor John Howie, academic who helped reform Scottish education - Obituaries |publisher=Scotsman.com |date= 23 January 2012 |accessdate=2012-01-23}}</ref>

==Biography==
Howie was educated at [[Robert Gordon's College]], [[Aberdeen]], the [[University of Aberdeen]] and [[Balliol College, Oxford]], where he wrote a Ph.D. thesis under the direction of [[Graham Higman]].

In 1966 the [[University of Stirling]] was established with [[Walter D. Munn]] ([[:fr:Walter D. Munn|fr]]) at head of the department of mathematics. Munn recruited Howie to teach there.<ref name=CH/>{{rp|290}}

According to Christopher Hollings,
:...a 'British school' of semigroup theory cannot be said to have taken off properly until the mid-1960s when John M. Howie completed an Oxford DPhil in semigroup theory (partly under [[Gordon Preston|Preston's]] influence) and Munn began to supervise research students in semigroups (most notably, Norman R. Reilly).<ref name=CH>{{citation |first=Christopher |last=Hollings|title=Mathematics across the Iron Curtain: A History of the Algebraic Theory of Semigroups|year=2014|page=185|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|isbn=978-1-4704-1493-1|zbl=1317.20001}}.</ref>

He won the [[Keith Prize]] of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]], 1979–81. He was [[Regius Professor of Mathematics]] at the [[University of St Andrews]] from 1970 to 1997. No successor to this chair was named until 2015 when [[Igor Rivin]] was appointed.

Howie was charged with reviewing universal, comprehensive [[secondary education]] in Scotland, which was viewed as failing its students. Impressed with [[education in Denmark]], his committee proposed a [[tracking (education)|tracking]] scheme to improve academic outcomes, and communicated recommendations in ''Upper Secondary Education in Scotland'' (1992).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.era.lib.ed.ac.uk/bitstream/handle/1842/9429/Chapter_1.pdf?sequence=4&isAllowed=y |title=Howie Report|publisher=[[University of Edinburgh]]}}</ref><ref>Andrew McPherson (1992) {{cite web |url=http://www.scottishgovernmentyearbooks.ed.ac.uk/record/23104/1/1992_9_TheHowieCommitteeonpost-compulsoryschooling.pdf|title= The Howie Committee on Post-compulsory Schooling|publisher= Scottish Government Yearbook}}</ref>

==Public appointments==
* Mathematics Panel, [[Scottish Examination Board]] 1967–1973; Convener from 1970
* Chairman, [[Scottish Central Committee for Mathematics]] 1975–1981
* President, [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]] 1973–74
* [[London Mathematical Society]]:
** Council 1982–1988, 1989–1992
** Vice-president 1986–1988, 1990–1992
** Chairman of Education Committee 1985–1989
** Chairman of Public Affairs Committee 1990–1992
* Member of [[Dunning Committee]] 1975–1977
* Chairman of Governors, [[Dundee College of Education]] 1983–1987
* Governor, [[Northern College of Education]] 1987–2001
* Chairman, [[Scottish Mathematical Council]] 1987–1993
* Chairman, Committee to review fifth and sixth years ([[Howie Committee]]) 1990–1992
* Council, [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] 1992–1995
* Chairman, Steering Committee, [[International Centre for Mathematical Sciences]] 1991–1997

==Books==
* 1976: ''An Introduction to Semigroup Theory'', [[Academic Press]] {{mr|id=0466355}}
* 1991: ''Automata and Languages'', [[Clarendon Press]] {{ISBN|0-19-853424-8}} {{mr|id=1254435}}
* 1992: ''Upper Secondary Education in Scotland'' (Howie Report)<ref>{{MacTutor|class=extras|id=Howie_comm.html|title=Howie Committee}}</ref>
* 1995: ''Fundamentals of Semigroup Theory'', Clarendon Press {{ISBN|0-19-851194-9}} {{mr|id=1455373}}
* 2001: ''Real Analysis'', [[Springer books]] {{ISBN|1-85233-314-6}} {{mr|id=1826051}}
* 2003: ''Complex Analysis'', Springer books {{ISBN|1-85233-733-8}} {{mr|id=1975725}}
* 2006: ''Fields and Galois Theory'', Springer books {{ISBN|978-1-85233-986-9}} {{mr|id=2180311}}
